newsitem.title: USA: Continental closes on $190 mln financing.
newsitem.headline: Continental closes on $190 mln financing.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc said Thursday it closed funding on $190 million in expansion financing at Houston's George Bush International Airport.

The financing was structured as an issue of tax exempt special facility revenue bonds by the City of Houston to be funded from the net rentals paid by Continental to the city under leases for the facilities.

The issue consisted of $74.2 million of Series 1997A bonds bearing interest at between 4.7 percent and six percent depending on maturity; $71.2 million of 6-1/8 percent Series 1997B bonds; and $44.6 million of 6-1/8 percent Series 1997C bonds.

The plan, which was undertaken a month ago, includes a $71 million renovation of Terminals B and C, the construction of a $74 million automated people mover to link the terminals, a $15 million mail sorting facility and a $30 million line maintenance facility, the company said.
The renovations, new facilities and the new people mover are scheduled for completion by the summer of 1999, it said.
